First, we note that using partial fractions, we have

$$
\frac{1}{(n-3)(n-2)}=\frac{1}{n-3}-\frac{1}{n-2}.
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
{\sum }_{n=7}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n-3}-\frac{1}{n-2}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{7} & =(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}) \\ {s}_{8} & =(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{6}) \\ {s}_{9} & =(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{7}) \\ {s}_{10} & =(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{8})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that for each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms except for the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{N} & =\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=7}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(n-3)(n-2)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{N-2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
